beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Anti-Idiocracy asks why accurate arguments lose to cultures that reward confident error.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its opening evolutionary debate shows a quick joke defeating a careful explanation.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book argues that correction needs belonging, practical support, and limits on authority.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It develops Outfinitism, a proposed discipline for studying where our models stop working.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its Outfinitist metacult would turn that discipline into shared practices and mutual support.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Members must remain free to challenge leaders without losing their place.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book makes this concrete through a hypothetical gathering around automated recruitment.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A founder brings an AI system designed to select job candidates.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A specialist asks which population was used to validate its predictions.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: An applicant asks who can appeal when those predictions reject someone.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The group also asks whether applicants retain a route without automated selection.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Each perspective exposes a different limit, turning model evaluation into questions of authority.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The chapters then ask how such a community could correct itself.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Founding texts must remain open to challenge, with changes recorded across editions.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Members can carry evidence of their contributions when leaving, while protecting private data.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Useful support might mean finding an independent evaluator or closing a project without stigma.
